title: Compositional Stability and Stepwise Improvement in the Hygienic Quality of Milk in a High-Andean Pasture-Based Dairy System
content: Seasonal variation in milk quality has been described mainly in temperate systems. We analysed the temporal dynamics of fat, protein, total bacterial count (TBC) and somatic cell count (SCC) in bulk tank milk from a crossbred Holstein herd grazing exclusively on a mixed sward of Trifolium repens, Plantago lanceolata, Lolium perenne and Pennisetum clandestinum at 2834 m a.s.l. in Ecuador, before and after the introduction of a milking parlour. Fifty-nine payment-for-quality results (2023–2026) were analysed with autocorrelation-corrected Mann–Kendall tests, Pettitt change-point detection, harmonic regression, segmented models, Spearman correlations, control charts and a monthly-mean sensitivity analysis. Fat (4.09 ± 0.31%) and protein (3.43 ± 0.11%) showed no trend or seasonality. TBC decreased by 0.40 log₁₀ per year, with geometric means of 82,600, 24,471 and 7841 CFU/mL in three successive phases, and all parlour records were below 100,000 CFU/mL. SCC decreased by 0.055 log₁₀ per year and never exceeded 400,000 cells/mL in any three-month window. Composition was not associated with hygiene indicators over the full series; in the parlour period, fat covaried with SCC (ρ = 0.67) without changes in protein, consistent with a concentration effect. The high-Andean forage system sustained a stable milk composition while hygienic quality improved progressively.
